optimizedDescription.value: Central Change entity enforces named spec-work lifecycle, approvals, artifacts, invalidation, implementation tracking, and append-only history.

optimizedContext.value:
# Change

## Rules

- Identity: unique immutable slug `name`; immutable `createdAt`. Reject whole-slug Windows device names on every OS, case-insensitive: `con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`–`com9`, `lpt1`–`lpt9`. Larger slugs such as `con-foo` stay legal when the slug pattern matches. Every event requires `ActorIdentity`: `name`, `email`, optional `provider`, `providerId`, `metadata: Record<string, string>`.
- Revision: persist `updatedAt`; default `createdAt`; never before `createdAt`. `touchUpdatedAt(at: Date = new Date())` sets or advances it.
- Scope: mutable, possibly empty `specIds`. At creation, validate the workspace component against `specd.yaml`; do not validate the spec path on the filesystem. `specIds` edits invalidate approvals. `workspaces` is a runtime getter via `parseSpecId()`; empty when `specIds` is empty; never persisted; plural touched set only — no home or primary workspace. Template variables and archive paths MUST NOT use `workspaces[0]` or any index as the change workspace. `specDependsOn` is an optional per-spec map and the highest-priority `CompileContext` `dependsOn` source, independent of `.specd-metadata.yaml`; updates do not append `invalidated`. `updateSpecIds()` drops keys absent from the new `specIds`. Other `dependsOn` links resolve dynamically and transitively from each spec `.specd-metadata.yaml` on every `CompileContext` run.
- Lifecycle (`VALID_TRANSITIONS`): `drafting → designing → ready → implementing ⇄ verifying → done → archivable → archiving`. Optional `approvals.spec` (default false) inserts `pending-spec-approval → spec-approved` between `ready` and `implementing`. Optional `approvals.signoff` (default false) inserts `pending-signoff → signed-off` between `done` and `archivable`. When `approvals.spec: true`, `ready → implementing` stays blocked until approval (`reason`, `artifactHashes`) reaches `spec-approved`; when false those states are unreachable and `ready → implementing` is free. When `approvals.signoff: true`, `done → archivable` stays blocked for new, modified, or removed specs until sign-off, then `signed-off → archivable`; when false `done → archivable` is free. Archive only from `archivable`; any other state throws `InvalidStateTransitionError`.
- From `archiving`, only `archivable` and `designing`; any other target throws `InvalidStateTransitionError`. Pre-commit failure (hooks, preflight, guards) stays `archivable` and never enters `archiving`. Commit failure attempts batch canonical restore: success does `archiving → archivable`; restore failure stays `archiving` until manual `designing`. `archiving → designing` remains the manual escape for spec or delta revision and for failed restore. After a successful archive move, metadata generation and post-archive hook failure do not undo archive. Success is not another active-history event; traceability lives on the archived record.
- Every state except `drafting` MAY return to `designing`, including `archiving`. `designing → designing` is re-entry and MUST NOT invalidate approvals or downgrade artifacts. Return from a later state does not imply drift; the artifact set must be reviewed again.
- `implementing → verifying` may repeat and is gated by workflow `taskCompletionCheck` because `verifying.requires` includes `tasks`. That check is artifact content, not approval state. `implementation-failure` returns `implementing` without invalidating or downgrading unchanged artifacts and resets only artifacts in `implementing.requires`. `artifact-review-required` returns `designing`. A validated file that becomes `drifted-pending-review` invalidates back to `designing` regardless of lifecycle state. `verifying → implementing` does not invalidate approvals.
- Implementation facts are separate from artifacts. `trackedImplementationFiles` are project-relative files with review state `open|resolved|ignored|removed`. `removed` stays in review history, is not implicit untrack, and is not reopened through `resolve`; it returns to `open` only when refresh confirms the file exists again. `implementationLinks` support file-level `spec -> file` and symbol refinements `spec -> file -> symbols`. Active paths stay project-relative; `workspace:path` normalization happens at archive materialization. Preserve explicit file-level link versus container-only set: removing the last symbol MAY drop a container-only set and MUST keep an explicitly created file-level link.
- `implementationTrackingStartedAt: Date | null`; `isImplementationTrackingActive` is true iff non-null. `startImplementationTracking(at?: Date)` records once and preserves the initial timestamp on later calls.
- Historical implementation signal: scan history for any `transitioned` event whose `to` is `implementing`. Once true, it stays true even if the current state leaves `implementing`. The entity performs no file detection. Draft and discard fail by default after this signal unless an explicit force override is supplied.
- Artifacts: schema-typed `ChangeArtifact` with `type`, `optional`, ordered `requires`, persisted aggregate `state`, and `files: Map<string, ArtifactFile>`. `scope: change` is typically one file keyed by artifact type id; `scope: spec` is one file per `specIds` entry. `ArtifactFile` has `key` (type id or spec ID), `filename`, explicit persisted `state`, `validatedHash`, and `hasDrift`. Hash uses schema `preHashCleanup`. `"__skipped__"` marks an explicit optional skip.
- Canonical states: `missing|in-progress|complete|skipped|pending-review|drifted-pending-review`. Explicit `state` plus current presence is authoritative. `validatedHash` is the last validated baseline only and does not prove the file still exists or is still complete. `missing` also covers backward-compatible loads with no persisted state. Aggregate priority: any `drifted-pending-review`; else any `pending-review`; else all `complete` or `skipped` with at least one file => `complete`; all `skipped` with a file => `skipped`; all `missing` or no files => `missing`; else `in-progress`. Effective `pending-parent-artifact-review`: a file stays blocked while an upstream artifact-DAG parent is `drifted-pending-review` or `pending-review`, recursively; aggregate applies when no file is drifted or `pending-review` and at least one file is `pending-parent-artifact-review`. Recursive blocker interpretation belongs to `LifecycleEngine`.
- Only `optional: true` artifacts may be `skipped`; skipping a required artifact throws. An actor must set skip explicitly. Only `complete` and `skipped` satisfy `requires`; `missing`, `in-progress`, `pending-review`, and `drifted-pending-review` block dependents. `ChangeArtifact.markComplete(key, hash)` is only from `ValidateArtifacts`: set file `complete`, update `validatedHash`, recompute the parent. `markSkipped()` marks ALL files and is only from the skip use case.
- Return to `designing`, or a scope change while already `designing`, stops treating previously validated files as `complete` until they are reviewed again. Files already `drifted-pending-review` keep that more specific state. Reopening inside `invalidate()` follows policy and is not always global.
- `syncArtifacts(artifactTypes)` compares the map with schema types, adds types and expected files from scope and `specIds`, removes types gone from the schema, adds or removes spec-scoped files to match `specIds`, and returns whether anything changed. On change it appends `artifacts-synced` (`typesAdded`, `typesRemoved`, `filesAdded`, `filesRemoved`) with `SYSTEM_ACTOR` `{ name: 'specd', email: 'system@getspecd.dev', provider: 'system' }`.
- History is append-only; events are never modified or deleted. Lifecycle state is the latest `transitioned.to`, otherwise `drafting`. Drafted iff the latest of `drafted|restored` is `drafted` (`drafts/` versus `changes/`). Active approval is the latest `spec-approved` or `signed-off` with no later `invalidated`. Common fields: `type`, ISO `at`, mandatory `by`. Events: `created` (`specIds`, `schemaName`, `schemaVersion`); `transitioned` (`from`, `to`); `spec-approved` and `signed-off` (`reason`, `artifactHashes`); `invalidated` (`cause`, `message`, `affectedArtifacts`); `drafted` (`reason?`); `restored`; `artifact-skipped` (`artifactId`, `reason?`); `artifacts-synced`; `description-updated` (`description`, via `EditChange --description`); `discarded` (`reason`, `supersededBy?`); `archive-failed` (`step: prepare|commit|archive`, `message`, `commitStarted`). `archive-failed` records the failed active attempt and does not itself complete archive.
- `invalidated.cause`: `spec-change` | `artifact-drift` | `artifact-review-required` | `spec-overlap-conflict`. `message` is a human explanation. `affectedArtifacts` entries are `{ type, files }`, using the file key for `scope: change` and the spec ID for `scope: spec`; dedupe targets. One drift pass records every drifted file on the same event. `spec-overlap-conflict` names the archived change and overlapping spec IDs and appends `transitioned` back to `designing` when that peer was archived with `allowOverlap: true`. Spec-list or artifact-content changes append `invalidated` then `transitioned` to `designing`, from use cases or `FsChangeRepository.get()` using `SYSTEM_ACTOR`.
- `created` stores the active `schemaName` and `schemaVersion`. `schema.name() !== change.schemaName` throws `SchemaMismatchError` before any work. A same-name `schemaVersion` mismatch warns; the change stays usable and archivable.
- Draft (`changes/` → `drafts/`) appends `drafted` (`by`, `at`, optional `reason`) without changing lifecycle state. Restore (`drafts/` → `changes/`) appends `restored` and only `RestoreChange` via `ChangeRepository.mutateDraft` may do it. Discard (`changes/` or `drafts/` → `discarded/`) appends `discarded` with mandatory `reason` and `by`, optional `supersededBy`, and is irreversible. Historical `implementing` makes draft and discard fail unless force is set.
- `isDrafted === true` means read-only. Forbidden: `transitioned` events, persisted validation, scope edits, approvals, invalidations, implementation-tracking updates, and transforming artifact writes. Allowed transforms: restore and discard through `mutateDraft`. Inspection uses `ChangeRepository.getDraft` or `GetDraft` and returns `DraftedChangeView`, not a mutable `Change`. Active-only resolution throws `ChangeNotFoundError`; an incorrect low-level persistence call throws `DraftedChangeReadOnlyError`.
- `Change.invalidate()` requires a cause, message, focused `affectedArtifacts`, and `artifactDag: ArtifactDag`, plus optional `invalidationPolicyOverride`. Effective policy is the override, otherwise persisted `invalidationPolicy`. It always appends `invalidated` and returns `designing` when the prior state was different. Reopen policy: `none` reopens nothing solely because of invalidation; `surgical` reopens the normalized target set; `downstream` reopens that set plus ids from `artifactDag.descendantsOf()` for the normalized target types; `global` reopens every artifact and file. Deduplicate before applying. Do not derive DAG edges from persisted `requires` or private BFS.
- `hasDrift` persists per file beside canonical state and the baseline hash. `true` means content differs or the file is absent; `false` means it matches the baseline. Set `true` only for cause `artifact-drift` and only the focused `affectedArtifacts`. Cause `artifact-review-required` neither sets nor clears it. Drifted files become `drifted-pending-review`; other files are not marked drifted unless their own validated content changed. `complete` with `hasDrift` MAY render as `complete-with-drift`. Canonical `missing` stays `missing` even when `hasDrift` is true.
- `Change` owns persisted facts: history, current state, artifact files, aggregate states, approvals, and invalidations. `LifecycleEngine` interprets the schema DAG, workflow `requires`, recursive parent blocking, approval-gate routing, step reachability, effective artifact status, and the next blocker. The entity does not embed schema knowledge for those questions.

## Constraints

- `name` and `createdAt` are immutable; whole-slug Windows device names are rejected on every OS; `updatedAt >= createdAt`.
- `workspaces` is derived, non-persisted, and plural; empty `specIds` is valid; no primary workspace for template variables or archive paths.
- History is immutable and lifecycle-authoritative; no state snapshot is stored.
- Artifact state is explicit; `validatedHash` is a baseline only; `hasDrift` is independent; reopening is policy-driven.
- `skipped` is optional-only and satisfies `requires`; `markComplete` only from `ValidateArtifacts`; `markSkipped` only from the skip use case.
- Archive only from `archivable`; both approval gates default false and are opt-in via `approvals` in `specd.yaml`.
- `verifying → implementing` never invalidates approvals and resets only `implementing.requires`.
- `designing → designing` does not invalidate approvals or downgrade artifacts.
- Draft or discard after historical `implementing` requires force; discard is irreversible and needs `reason` and `by`.
- Effective blocker and workflow interpretation belong only to `LifecycleEngine`.
